newsitem.title: IRAN: Key facts about Iran and its presidential election.
newsitem.headline: Key facts about Iran and its presidential election.

text.p: Iran goes to the polls on Friday to elect a successor to President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani.
Here are key facts about the country and the election:

POPULATION: 60.6 million according to official figures but 69.9 million according to the United Nations. Comprises many ethnic groups of Aryan or Turkic descent including Kurds, with some Arabs in the south.
RELIGION: Mostly Shi'ite Moslem, with some Sunni Moslems, Baha'is, Orthodox Christians, Jews and Zoroastrians.
AREA: 1,684,184 sq km (650,264 sq miles), bordered by Afghanistan, Armenia, Azerbaijan, Iraq, Pakistan, Turkey and Turkmenistan. Southern coast extends from the head of the Gulf to the Indian Ocean.
CAPITAL: Tehran, population 6.6 million according to the 1996 census.

ECONOMY: Gross domestic product 186.125 trillion rials. Consumer inflation was 23.2 percent in urban areas in the Iranian year to March 20. Iran is heavily dependent on oil export revenue. It has 90 billion barrels of proven oil reserves, about 10 percent of the world total. Daily output is about 3.6 million barrels. Carpets are second most important export and pistachio nuts third.
UNEMPLOYMENT RATE: 10.7 percent but official figures disguise high under-employment and the fact many Iranian workers rely on income from at least two jobs.
EXCHANGE RATE: Official rate for calculating state budget account is $1=1,750 rials. Export rate is $1=3,000.
ARMED FORCES: 513,000, about half of whom are conscripts. Equipment includes 1,440 tanks, 295 combat aircraft including 30 MiG-29s, and three Russian Kilo-class submarines.
ELECTORAL SYSTEM: Winner must gain absolute majority of more than half of all votes. If no clear winner emerges on ballot there will be a runoff between the top two.
VOTING HOURS: 8 a.m. to 7 p.m. (0330-1430 GMT).

CANDIDATES: Mohammad Khatami, 54, former minister of culture and Islamic guidance; Ali Akbar Nateq-Nouri, 54, speaker of the Majlis (parliament); Mohammad Mohammadi Reyshahri, 51, former prosecutor general and revolutionary Iran's first intelligence minister; Reza Zavarei, 59, deputy head of the judiciary. All are Shi'ite Moslems. Only Zavarei is not a clergyman.
PREVIOUS ELECTION: In the sixth presidential election in June 1993, 16,789,666 votes were cast with 10,555,912 or 63.2 percent going to the incumbent Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani.
